answer: In a shared garden registry, each identity adopts one vine in a grove and logs its growth weekly: shoot lengths, leaf counts, every pruning cut. Rewards follow the continuity of that private history, spot-checked against dated photos and neighbours whose vines intertwine with it. A sybil operator can copy a log once, but the copy then diverges from the real plant, and maintaining fifty divergent, internally consistent histories costs fifty real seasons of tending. A fresh clone starts years behind, earning nothing until time itself, not text, has accumulated.
